interest: This file is particularly valuable for historians of occupied Japan and U.S. diplomatic recordkeeping because of its combination of technical industrial data and archival misfiling. The 1949 ramie report by the Toyo Sen-i Company offers rich technical and agricultural insight into the revival of Japan's textile fiber industry under SCAP, detailing smallholder cultivation practices, non-chemical decortication technologies, and processing workflows, while revealing that the inquiry originated with the Spanish Diplomatic Mission in Tokyo. The despatch was drafted by Edward G. Seidensticker, Jr., then a young foreign service officer who would later become one of the premier American translators and scholars of Japanese literature. Furthermore, the accidental consolidation of 1945–1946 tobacco correspondence with Edwin W. Pauley's Reparations Mission—caused by a Division of Central Records (DCR) catch sheet—provides a fascinating window into early post-war commercial overtures by Egyptian merchants seeking barter trade (Egyptian raw cotton and fertilizers for Japanese leaf tobacco) before regular private international commerce had normalized.
overview: This file (decimal 894.61325, covering May 13, 1946 to July 25, 1949) consists of two distinct groups of records bound together due to an internal State Department filing cross-reference. The primary subject is post-war Japanese ramie fiber cultivation and processing, represented by Despatch No. 480 (July 25, 1949) from the Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan in Tokyo, which transmits a comprehensive technical report prepared by the Toyo Sen-i Company for the Economic and Scientific Section of GHQ, SCAP at the request of the Spanish Diplomatic Mission. The second, earlier group consists of a 1946 Division of Central Records (DCR) catch sheet and 1945–1946 correspondence from Egyptian merchants Emmanuel Frankel (The Nile Commercial Company) and Raphael S. Soussi to Ambassador Edwin W. Pauley of the Allied Commission on Reparations, proposing to purchase or barter for Japanese unmanufactured leaf tobacco in exchange for Egyptian cotton and phosphates or as reparations payments.

subfiles.about: Cover despatch forwarding a technical report on Japanese ramie production compiled by Toyo Sen-i Company for SCAP at the request of the Spanish Diplomatic Mission.
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (drafted by Edward G. Seidensticker, Jr.)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 480 from the Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan in Tokyo transmits to the Department of State and Department of Commerce a technical report on ramie production in Japan. The report was compiled for SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section by the Toyo Sen-i Company of Tokyo. The despatch highlights that the study was originally requested by the Spanish Diplomatic Mission on behalf of Spanish ramie producers.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 480 from Tokyo Forwarding Report on Ramie

subfiles.about: Detailed technical report on ramie seed types, cultivation yields, decortication machinery, and spinning and weaving processes in Japan.
subfiles.summary: This technical report details the agricultural and mechanical processes of the Japanese ramie industry. It outlines seed varieties (Hakuhi, Saikei, Seishin), multi-annual cutting cycles, regional yields between Southern and Northern Japan, and specific fertilizer requirements for smallholder plots averaging 0.1 hectare. It describes non-chemical fiber extraction using Ikeda, Kiyofuji, and Tosen decorticators, and outlines the stages of industrial spinning and weaving for products such as suiting, canvas, and fish netting.
subfiles.title: Report on Ramie by Toyo Sen-i Company
subfiles.to: Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ, SCAP

subfiles.about: Administrative charge-out sheet requesting Alexandria Telegram 55 of May 13, 1946 for transfer between State Department decimal files.
subfiles.from: Mrs. Collins, Division of Central Records (DC/R)
subfiles.summary: This Department of State Division of Central Records (DCR) catch sheet records a charge-out by Mrs. Collins for Telegram 55 of May 13, 1946 from Alexandria. The slip notes that the document is being transferred from file 894.6133/5-1346 to file 894.61331/5-1346. Its placement in this folder explains the May 13, 1946 start date on the file cover and the presence of subsequent tobacco-related records.
subfiles.title: DCR Catch Sheet for Telegram 55 from Alexandria

subfiles.about: Business contact slip listing the Alexandria and Cairo offices of Emmanuel Frankel, Managing Director of The Nile Commercial Company.
subfiles.from: Emmanuel Frankel, Managing Director, The Nile Commercial Company
subfiles.summary: A printed calling card or business slip for Emmanuel Frankel, Managing Director of The Nile Commercial Company. It provides contact addresses and telephone numbers for the company's offices on Falaki Street in Alexandria and Sharia Malika Farida in Cairo, Egypt. It serves as contact information attached to Frankel's correspondence regarding Japanese tobacco imports.
subfiles.title: Business Calling Card of Emmanuel Frankel

subfiles.about: Letter inquiring whether the U.S. Reparations Commission is interested in exporting Japanese and Korean leaf tobacco to Egypt and proposing a meeting in Washington.
subfiles.summary: Writing from Montreal, Emmanuel Frankel of The Nile Commercial Company follows up on an inquiry sent by Raphael S. Soussi of Alexandria regarding the sale of Japanese leaf tobacco in Egypt. Frankel requests that Edwin W. Pauley inform him in New York whether the proposal is of interest to the U.S. government. He offers to travel to Washington between January 5 and 12, 1946, to discuss the transaction in person.
subfiles.title: Letter from Emmanuel Frankel to Edwin W. Pauley regarding Japanese and Korean Leaf Tobacco
subfiles.to: Edwin W. Pauley, Head of Far Eastern Reparations Commission, Department of State

subfiles.about: Letter acknowledging that Soussi's prior communication regarding Japanese leaf tobacco will be forwarded to Ambassador Pauley upon his return to the U.S.
subfiles.summary: Raphael S. Soussi of Alexandria writes to Edwin W. Pauley acknowledging an interim letter of November 28, 1945 from the Allied Commission on Reparations. Soussi notes that his initial proposal of November 10 arrived during Pauley's absence from the country and expresses satisfaction that it will now be submitted directly to him. He states that he looks forward to receiving a favorable response regarding Japanese leaf tobacco.
subfiles.title: Letter from Raphael S. Soussi to Edwin W. Pauley regarding Japanese Leaf Tobacco
subfiles.to: Edwin W. Pauley, Allied Commission on Reparations, The White House

subfiles.about: Letter confirming a telegraphic offer to purchase Japanese leaf tobacco via cash or barter for Egyptian cotton and phosphates as reparations payments.
subfiles.summary: Raphael S. Soussi confirms a cable sent to Ambassador Edwin W. Pauley urging a prompt decision on purchasing available stocks or future crops of Japanese unmanufactured tobacco. Soussi explains that Japanese leaf is traditionally consumed in Egypt for Turkish-blend cigarettes and will not compete with American Virginia tobacco. He proposes purchasing available stocks either for foreign currency (Sterling, Egyptian pounds, or U.S. dollars) or through barter exchange for Egyptian raw cotton and fertilizer phosphates needed in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Raphael S. Soussi to Edwin W. Pauley proposing Purchase or Barter of Japanese Tobacco
subfiles.to: Edwin W. Pauley, Ambassador, Allied Commission on Reparations, The White House
